classification.difficultyReason: Solve trigonometric equations within the restricted interval, classify stationary points and verify concavity changes, then assemble a sketch through the endpoints and calculated features.

content.prompt: Consider the curve $y=\sin x+\cos x$ in the interval $0\le x\le2\pi$.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Find the values of the function at the endpoints of the domain.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}\sin x+\cos x&=0\\\sin x&=-\cos x\\\tan x&=-1\\x&=\frac{3\pi}{4},\frac{7\pi}{4}.\end{align*}$$
The intercepts are $\left(\frac{3\pi}{4},0\right)$ and $\left(\frac{7\pi}{4},0\right)$.

children.label: c
children.prompt: Find any stationary points and determine their nature.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}f'(x)&=\cos x-\sin x\\\cos x-\sin x&=0\\\tan x&=1\\x&=\frac{\pi}{4},\frac{5\pi}{4}\\f\left(\frac{\pi}{4}\right)&=\sqrt2\\f\left(\frac{5\pi}{4}\right)&=-\sqrt2.\end{align*}$$
The signs of $f'(x)$ on $\left(0,\frac{\pi}{4}\right)$, $\left(\frac{\pi}{4},\frac{5\pi}{4}\right)$ and $\left(\frac{5\pi}{4},2\pi\right)$ are $+$, $-$ and $+$. Thus $\left(\frac{\pi}{4},\sqrt2\right)$ is a maximum and $\left(\frac{5\pi}{4},-\sqrt2\right)$ is a minimum.

children.label: d
children.prompt: Find any points of inflection and sketch the curve.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}f''(x)&=-\sin x-\cos x\\-\sin x-\cos x&=0\\x&=\frac{3\pi}{4},\frac{7\pi}{4}.\end{align*}$$
The concavity changes from down to up at $x=\frac{3\pi}{4}$ and from up to down at $x=\frac{7\pi}{4}$. Thus both $x$-intercepts are points of inflection. Sketch through the endpoints $(0,1)$ and $(2\pi,1)$, the stationary points and the intercepts.
